title: Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M — Atomic Chat on an 8 GB laptop GPU
slug_note: 2.71 GB file on an RTX 4060 / 4060 Laptop: full-model-on-VRAM with ~4 GB left for KV cache.

variation.quant_detail: qwen35-4b-Q4_K_M.gguf (2.71 GB, HF tree), self-quantized from Qwen's original weights with a per-tensor imatrix

engine.config: Atomic Chat app on Windows or Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU; llama.cpp backend inside the app. Model found by searching AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF and picking Q4_K_M. Backend/context not stated.

requirements.notes: Estimate: 2.71 GB Q4_K_M file + 8192-token KV headroom ≈ 3.5 GB, which stays inside the card's 7.5 GB usable VRAM (NVIDIA 8 GB class).

steps.text: Install Atomic Chat from https://atomic.chat/ (Linux x86_64 and Windows x64 downloads listed on the homepage).
Open the app, search AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF, pick a quant, hit Use this model.
Start chatting; the app runs the GGUF on its bundled engine.

caveats: No laptop measurement recorded: status untested. The card's same-model Q4_K_M command ran as written on our DGX Spark on 2026-11-16 via llama.cpp; that box's speeds do not carry over to an 8 GB laptop GPU.
The AtomicChat GGUF repo ships text-only quants — it carries no vision projector, so this lane has no image input.
Atomic Chat has three swappable backends (see the engine record's gotchas); no speed is claimed here, so attribution does not bind.
